entities.name: Query 301 aa riboflavin enzyme
observations: The 301-residue sequence has estimated molecular mass 34.43 kDa and theoretical pI 8.49.
Pfam detects PRA-CH (PF01502) at residues 27–101 and GTP_cyclohydro2 (PF00925) at residues 118–277.
The C-terminal region matches RibA/GTP cyclohydrolase II homologs at about 50–56% identity over roughly 186–196 residues.
The sequence lacks a hydrophobic N-terminal segment suggestive of a signal peptide or membrane anchor; soluble localization is inferred from sequence architecture.

The fused PRA-CH plus GTP_cyclohydrolase II architecture is consistent with a bacterial riboflavin-biosynthesis protein, likely RibBA-like, but exact annotation is not experimentally established for this query.

entities.name: RibA GTP cyclohydrolase II
observations: RibA/GTP cyclohydrolase II is the homolog family represented by the strongest C-terminal sequence matches, including UniProt hit P0A7I8 and related RIBA entries.

This enzyme catalyzes the first committed step of riboflavin biosynthesis, converting GTP toward 3,4-dihydroxy-2-butanone 4-phosphate and a pterin-derived product; exact reaction details were not directly retrieved for the query.

entities.name: Riboflavin biosynthesis
observations: The sequence architecture supports likely participation in bacterial riboflavin biosynthesis through a RibA-like GTP cyclohydrolase II domain.
This pathway assignment is homology/domain based rather than a curated annotation of the query sequence.
